entry.title: Westside Gunn Announces New Album Heelmatic
entry.summary: Lead single “Zilla” features rapping on a camel in front of the Great Pyramid
entry.content:
Wrestling fanatic/Buffalo ad-lib king Westside Gunn is back with a new album called, naturally, Heelmatic. It arrives with a video of lead single “Zilla,” which was shot on location in Egypt. The clip technically premiered on Instagram back in August, but we’re showcasing it here since it just hit YouTube. Behold as Gunn rides a camel in Cairo then in front of the Great Pyramid while he raps about Oakleys, Glocks, and “choppin' bricks karate type.”

“ALBUM OTW AND ITS ALL GRIMEY, DUSTY, SOULFUL, JAZZ INSPIRED mixed with FLYEST SHIT U EVER HEARD IN YA LIFE,” he wrote in a post teasing the album this summer. Heelmatic is out November 13 on Griselda Records/Mass Appeal.

Westside Gunn will be heading overseas shortly after the album’s release, for his Heel the World Tour 2: “Still Healing” trek. Those dates, across the UK and Europe, can be found below, along with the Heelmatic tracklist and album artwork. Gunn’s last full-length releases were a trio of 2025 mixtapes: 12, Heels Have Eyes 2, and Heels Have Eyes 3.

entry.title: The Strokes and Phoebe Bridgers to Play SNL
entry.summary: Oh and also Gracie Abrams
entry.content:
Saturday Night Live has revealed the musical guests for its first November episodes. The Strokes will return to the Studio 8H stage on November 6 opposite first-time host Druski. The following week, Phoebe Bridgers will give her first solo SNL performance (Boygenius were musical guests in 2023) since the great guitar smashing fiasco of 2021, on a John Mulaney-hosted episode.

SNL’s 52nd season has already featured performances from Rosalía, Turnstile, and Katseye. Taylor Swift also made a surprise appearance during the October 3 episode to present that week’s host, Dakota Johnson, with a birthday cake. After taking the weekend off, SNL will return on Halloween with Obsession’s Inde Navarrette hosting and Gracie Abrams performing.

Revisit the reviews of Phoebe Bridgers’ new album Lost Weekend, named Best New Music, and the Strokes’ new album Reality Awaits, not named Best New Music.

entry.title: Fleetwood Mac Announce Fleetwood Mac Documentary
entry.summary: Fleetwood Mac: The Chain hits Apple TV in January
entry.content:
The story of Fleetwood Mac is classic rock canon at this point, memorialized via an assortment of unauthorized films, loosely inspired TV shows and plays, and Lindsey Buckingham’s recent turn as a reaction influencer for some reason. Now the band themselves are ready to “officially” tell their story, in Fleetwood Mac: The Chain, a Frank Marshall-directed documentary. It’s set to premiere on Apple TV on January 29.

Unsurprisingly, The Chain will keep its focus on the most popular era of the Mac: their 1974-2018 lineup of Stevie Nicks, Buckingham, Mick Fleetwood, John McVie, and the late Christine McVie. (Sorry to Peter Green heads). The Chain, which promises “never-before-seen footage and exclusive new interviews,” bills itself as the first fully authorized documentary from the band, though that’s a bit of a technicality: they all participated in the BBC’s one-hour 2009 doc Fleetwood Mac: Don’t Stop.

You can watch the very short teaser trailer for the new one below.

entry.title: Kacey Musgraves Reveals Middle of Nowhere Companion Album

Billed as Middle of Nowhere Vol. 2: Tex Mex Tapes, the 16-track release consists of 11 new songs and 5 covers, including a Spanish rendition of “Uncertain, TX” from the original record. It’s out January 15 via Lost Highway. Tonight, Musgraves will share “Weekend in Texas” and her version of the norteño standard “Mi Tesoro.” For now, check out the cover art and tracklist below.

Middle of Nowhere was led by the single “Dry Spell” and its title track. Since its May release, Musgraves has also shared a video for “Mexico Honey.” She’s currently winding down her North American tour in support of the album, which wraps up with two shows at Climate Pledge Arena in Seattle on October 26 and 27.

entry.title: Being Dead Sign to Polyvinyl, Plan to “Take Over the World”
entry.summary: The Austin rock trio has also shared two new songs, one about dating a dolphin
entry.content:
Being Dead have signed to Polyvinyl and shared their first songs in two years. “Man or Myth” is the Austin rock trio ode’s to Marc Ornstein, a famed “interpretive freestyle” canoeist, while “Aquarium” is about “the taboo nature of falling in love in the workplace, which is especially scandalous if the workplace is an aquarium and your coworker is a dolphin,” according to the band. Both come with music videos directed by Being Dead’s own Falcon Bitch, which you can watch below.

“We don’t mean to put too much pressure on Polyvinyl,” Being Dead said in press materials, “but if we’re not inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame within the next two years, we’re throwing in the towel. That said, we have full confidence that together, we will take over the world.”

“Man or Myth / Aquarium” follows 2024’s Eels, Being Dead’s John Congleton-produced sophomore LP. Congleton also returned to work on both new songs.

Read about Eels at No. 38 in The 50 Best Albums of 2024.

entry.title: Daft Punk Are Now Lego
entry.summary: And so is the Alive 2007 pyramid
entry.content:
We’re probably no closer to a Daft Punk reunion five years after the duo broke up—this despite completely unfounded rumors plus a run of legacy-building post-breakup projects—but now you can at least pretend Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo are playing at your house thanks to Lego’s latest collection. The Daft Punk set can be traced back to Covid lockdown, when a father and son from Luxembourg suggested the company recreate the duo’s 2007 Alive Tour pyramid stage. A rendering of that model can be found below, along with the DJ duo's official Lego minifigures. Bangalter and Homem-Christo now join the Beatles and the Spice Girls in the annals of musicians who’ve become plastic bricks.

“The pyramid stage is one of the most recognisable expressions of Daft Punk’s visual world, so it feels fitting that this fan-created design will be centre stage of this partnership,” longtime Daft Punk creative director Cédric Hervet said in a statement. “Fans have always played an important part in Daft Punk’s story, and we are excited to see that creativity reflected through the LEGO universe.”

entry.title: Talking Heads Announce New Book
entry.summary: With essays from Lorde, Debbie Harry, Karl Ove Knausgaard, and more
entry.content:
Talking Heads are getting the band back together—for a new book. David Byrne, Tina Weymouth, Jerry Harrison, and Chris Frantz have announced Talking Heads: New Feeling, set to arrive on May 18. The release date also marks the 50th anniversary of the group’s debut album, Talking Heads: 77.

“For this book, we pulled out handwritten lyrics, original album sketches, and private photos, some of which haven’t left our archive in over 40 years,” Harrison told publisher Abrams Books in an interview today. New Feeling features original essays from all four members, plus contributions from Lorde, Debbie Harry, Karl Ove Knausgaard, Jeff Bridges, and more.

The new book also gathers behind-the-scenes photos from the 1984 concert film Stop Making Sense, which returned to theaters for a limited engagement in 2023. In an interview ahead of that re-release, Harrison told Pitchfork’s Andy Cush that seeing the film again “revives the joy we had together,” adding: ”It’s certainly tugging on the heartstrings of how much I loved everybody." Prior to promoting the film’s remaster, the band had not made an appearance together in decades.

It’s been a big month for Talking Heads fans. On October 1, the group detailed plans to share a freshly remastered, super-deluxe edition of their third album Fear of Music, That LP, coming November 13 on Rhino, expands the original track list with a number of alternate versions, studio outtakes, and previously unreleased full recordings of two concerts from the era. Its release will coincide with the launch of a new SiriusXM station dedicated to the band.

entry.title: Watch Fontaines D.C. Perform on Jools Holland
entry.summary: The Irish rock band broke out Dopamine Chamber songs and more for their special 45-minute set
entry.content:
The British TV institution Later… With Jools Holland has devoted a special episode to Fontaines D.C. The Irish band staged the performance at Alexandra Palace Theatre last week, performing songs from new album Dopamine Chamber. Watch them do “Mimesis,” “Tongue,” “You Miss Me,” and their 2024 radio hit “Favourite” below. The full, 45-minute set is available now to UK viewers on BBC iPlayer.

As the band continues to promote Dopamine Chamber, frontman Grian Chatten has addressed fallout after AI studios were credited in the making of their “Marianne” video. As Chatten tells it, the band only learned of the AI use after the video’s release. “All those main scenes and main effects and stuff were VFX and prosthetics, like the cheeks and everything,” he told The Los Angeles Times’ Julius Miller. “Over 110 people worked on the thing. It was a real huge human effort. But then somewhere in the process, someone from the VFX team I guess used some kind of AI in the workflow. And none of us were told about it. Apparently, not even our label or our management were told about it and it was a real shock.”

He said the band would prevent future snafus by writing an AI ban into contracts. “I was hoping to talk about how I felt about AI in interviews at some point anyway, and then this kind of pulled the rug from under that conversation a little bit,” he said, adding (and here we honor the LA Times’ house style on expletives) that AI in general is “f— terrifying. I was watching a Robin Williams scene from Dead Poets Society when he talks about poetry, literature. These are the things that we stay alive for, and well, that’s exactly what AI threatens to rob from the human race. I’ve seen those articles about those guys who are leaving AI companies because they said that the human race is going to be dead within 10 years. AI is literally rendering our souls obsolete and I think that is true death.”

Next year, Fontaines D.C. head out on a massive headlining tour across North America, Europe, Australia, and a few dates in Japan. Read Pitchfork’s review of Dopamine Chamber.

entry.title: Yung Miami Reveals Full Tracklist for Debut Solo Album
entry.summary: The long-awaited Watch Dis features Quavo, G Herbo, Lil Baby, Kodak Black, Shenseea, Vybez Kartel, and more
entry.content:
Two years after City Girls officially split to focus on their respective solo careers, Yung Miami has finally announced the arrival of her debut album, Watch Dis. She’s leading the LP with two new singles: “F U” and “2008.” Below, you can now check out the full tracklist, which reveals additional guests including Summer Walker and Travis Scott. And why not run back “Spend Dat” while you’re at it?

On Thursday, September 30 Yung Miami shared an appropriately dramatic trailer for the long-teased LP. The clip opens with public criticism she has faced from Joe Budden along with Akademiks—who comments, “You failed at everything in life, the music you made is wack”—before Miami responds, “I don’t know how some days I built the courage to go in the studio to even record. But I remember putting all my emotions, all of that energy, everything that I felt, into this album.”

Pitchfork previously revealed that Watch Dis will premiere October 23 and include features from Quavo, G Herbo, Lil Baby, Kodak Black, Shenseea, Vybez Kartel, and more. We also debuted the cover art. “I could’ve come back with one song and played it safe, but why?” Yung Miami said in a statement to Pitchfork. “I’m confident in what I made. I’m back to pop my shit and I want everybody to watch dis.”

Yung Miami has shared a stream of tracks in 2026, including the chart-topping, song-of-summer contender “Spend Dat.” In 2023 she released RAW with JT, the last album under the City Girls alias. Following the duo’s split, Miami focused on her Careesha Please talk show, which debuted its last season in 2024.

entry.title: Chvrches Announce First Album in Six Years and 2027 Tour
entry.summary: The trio will perform material from All The King’s Men on the road come spring
entry.content:
Chvrches are back with their first new album in six years. All The King’s Men arrives January 22 via Futures Music Group, and the band plans to tour extensively in support of it next year. Leading the LP is the single “Roses,” which Chvrches dropped last month.

Lauren Mayberry, Iain Cook, and Martin Doherty paused after touring behind their last album, 2021’s Screen Violence, to regroup and find a way to challenge themselves writing its follow-up. All The King’s Men is the result of those songwriting sessions: 11 indie rock songs that take inspiration from Massive Attack, PJ Harvey, Nick Drake, Bert Jansch, and Incredible String Band.

After All The King’s Men comes out, Chvrches will tour across the United States, Canada, England, Ireland, and their native Scotland, beginning on February 13 and lasting on through May 6. Check out their complete list of tour dates below.

entry.title: Snoh Aalegra Unveils New Album With Song Featuring Nile Rodgers and Raphael Saadiq
entry.summary: Listen to “I Love You” from Legendary Love
entry.content:
Snoh Aalegra is teeing up her first album in half a decade, Legendary Love. The announcement comes with a song called “I Love You,” for which the Iranian Swedish artist has recruited two legends from opposite corners of the R&B pantheon: Nile Rodgers on guitar and Raphael Saadiq on bass. Check out “I Love You” below, with a video directed by Alfred Marroquín. The album arrives November 13 via Stem.

Aalegra said of the new LP in a press release: “I don’t think the greatest love stories are measured by how long they last. They’re measured by who they ask you to become. Every song holds a piece of who I was, who I became, and who I will continue to be because I allowed myself to love this deeply. This love brought me back to the era of music I fell in love with growing up. It carried the same longing, romance, and nostalgia that first made me dream of becoming an artist.”

“I Love You,” which Aalegra co-wrote with Joel Compass and co-produced with Compass and Josh Grant, follows the release last week of “Karma,” her first song in three years. Her last LP was Temporary Highs in the Violet Skies.

entry.title: Angine de Poitrine Set 2027 International Tour
entry.summary: Will they land Angine de Pawtrine to open?
entry.content:
Angine de Poitrine haven’t even wrapped up their ongoing tour but they’re already plotting another. The Quebecois math rock duo will get right back on the road come March, beginning with their first-ever Australian stops. From there they’ll hop around to festival dates and headlining shows across South America, Canada, the U.S., Europe, and the UK. The run includes three nights at Brooklyn Steel in New York, then closes back in Angine de Poitrine’s home country with two July dates at Toronto’s RBC Amphitheatre and Chicoutimi’s Zone Portuaire.

Since the release of their latest album, Vol. II, back in April, Angine de Poitrine’s polka-dotted visages have become nigh inescapable. They performed on both Later… With Jools Holland and The Tonight Show With Jimmy Fallon, and were recently awarded the 2026 Polaris Music Prize. However, nothing else has proven their cultural omnipresence like the “Angine de Pawtrine” costume that made waves at the Tompkins Square Halloween Dog Parade this past weekend.

entry.title: Wendy Eisenberg Shares 30-Minute Song, Announces New Band With More Eaze
entry.summary: Whait will release their debut LP in February
entry.content:
Singer-songwriter and guitar virtuoso Wendy Eisenberg is back with a surprise release and a new band. The first, the companion work Wweennddyy Eeiisseennbbeerrgg, reimagines “Meaning Business” and “The Walls”—both of which appear on their recent self-titled album—into sprawling live renditions totaling 46 minutes. The two-song package was recorded with Mr. Bungle bassist Trevor Dunn, drummer Ryan Sawyer, and violinist Mari Rubio aka More Eaze.

Describing why they felt compelled to record alternate versions of the two tracks, Eisenberg said, “I want to write songs that feel infinite. I want to write songs that transcend their production, that can weather the changes. It’s probably a holdover from my jazz training, the desire to hear my material in different contexts. A standard sounds different passed through time and hands. This band, Ryan, Mari, and Trevor, can do anything — between them their practices span jazz, metal, country, ambient music, minimalism, and hyperpop, at least. Why not literally stretch them, and my songs, out? I want to feel when a slowed-down song becomes ambient music, becomes jazz, becomes something else. Experimental music; an experiment. Hopefully not chopped, but definitely a little screwed.”

Speaking of More Eaze, they will also join Eisenberg in the duo’s new band Whait. Their debut album, Sympathy at Home, drops February 17 via Night School Records. You can check out their first song together, “Falling down,” along with the reworks of “Mmeeaanniinngg Bbuussiinneessss” and “Tthhee Wwaallllss” below.

Read about Wendy Eisenberg in The Best Music of 2026 So Far.

entry.title: Bicep Reveal First Album in Five Years, Drop Three New Songs
entry.summary: Slug features contributions from Lauren Duffus, Eartheater, George Riley, Clark, and Sassy 009
entry.content:
Northern Irish DJ duo Bicep have revealed details of their first album in five years. Slug arrives January 29 via Ninja Tune. Last month, Bicep shared three singles from the LP—“Air,” “Lemonder,” and “Viper”—and they’ve dropped another triptych alongside today’s announcement: “Gas,” featuring Lauren Duffus and Soarr; “Ultra,” featuring Eartheater and Saskia; and “Equarium,” featuring Kehina. The songs come with music videos directed by Young Replicant, which together form a short film about pigeon fanciers. Watch below.

The title Slug was inspired, according to press materials, by “the stark contrast between the land slug most people immediately picture and the extraordinary colours, shapes and intricate forms of their underwater counterparts.” “For this album we really wanted to massively broaden what we do,” they added in an accompanying statement. “We wanted to make a much more varied album than our previous ones and push what people might expect BICEP to sound like.”

Slug will mark Bicep’s follow-up to 2021’s Isles. The album features additional contributions from Clark, George Riley, and Sassy 009, among others. Bicep have also lined up a pair of new 2027 live dates: one at New York’s Knockdown Center on March 21, and one at London’s Old Royal Naval College on July 31.

Revisit Ben Cardew’s review of Isles.
